precepts.text: Balaam the son of Beor was slain with the sword beside the five kings of Midian; the Midianites were his people.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“And now, behold, I go unto my people.” Who were Balaam's people? The Midianites. When Israel went against Midian, “they slew the kings of Midian, beside the rest of them that were slain; namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.”

Balaam died with the sword beside the five kings of Midian; that is the people he went unto.

precepts.text: These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor.
precepts.point: They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Israel abode in Shittim, “and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself.

Moses names it after the war with Midian: “Have ye saved all the women alive? Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.”

The daughters that called Israel to the sacrifices of their gods were sent by the counsel of Balaam. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.

precepts.text: The people began whoredom with the daughters of Moab and were joined unto Baal-peor; that history is the reason the Lord commanded the vengeance.
precepts.point: The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25; go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.
precepts.why:
“Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites.” The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.”

“And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” The whoredom with the daughters of the other nations and the joining unto Baal-peor is what Midian did to Israel, and it is why the Lord commanded Moses to avenge the children of Israel before he was gathered unto his people.

precepts.text: Phinehas took a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed.
precepts.point: Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of Numbers 25.
precepts.why:
Twelve thousand armed for war, a thousand of every tribe, went to the war with “Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest”, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow in his hand. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation in the history of Numbers 25.

“And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.”

The priest who stayed the plague with a javelin is the priest sent with the army to avenge the Lord of Midian.

precepts.text: Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.
precepts.point: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.
precepts.why:
They slew all the males and the five kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, and “Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.” Joshua tells who Balaam was: “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.”

Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak. That is the man Israel slew with the sword among the Midianites.

precepts.text: Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand; that plague in the matter of Peor is why the women who had known man could not be kept.
precepts.point: Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.
precepts.why:
Moses was wroth with the officers of the host because they saved all the women alive. “Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.” Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death.

“And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.” That plague in the matter of Peor is why every woman that had known man by lying with him could not be kept, and every male among the little ones was killed.

The women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

precepts.text: Put out of the camp every one defiled by the dead; the seven days without the camp keep that law.
precepts.point: Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.
precepts.why:
Those “whosoever hath killed any person, and whosoever hath touched any slain” had to abide without the camp seven days. That is the law going back to the start of the wilderness: “Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead.”

The men of war had touched the slain, so they were defiled by the dead and stayed outside the camp until they were purified. The seven days without the camp keep the law of Numbers 5.

precepts.text: He that touches the dead purifies himself on the third day and on the seventh day; the men of war purified themselves by that law.
precepts.point: Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.
precepts.why:
The men of war were to “purify both yourselves and your captives on the third day, and on the seventh day.” That is the law of purification: “He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days. He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean: but if he purify not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.”

The purifying of the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats’ hair and all things made of wood goes back to the same law of Numbers 19. Then Eleazar gave the ordinance for the spoil: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they washed their clothes, were clean, and came into the camp.

precepts.text: All the heave offerings of the holy things are given to the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; it is a covenant of salt before the Lord.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.
precepts.why:
Moses gave the tribute, “which was the Lord’s heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest.” It went to the priest by law: “All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto the Lord, have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord unto thee and to thy seed with thee.”

The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by a statute for ever, a covenant of salt. The Lord’s heave offering out of the spoil of Midian was Eleazar’s by that covenant.

precepts.text: Aaron has no inheritance in their land; the Lord is his part and his inheritance among the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.
precepts.why:
Why do the heave offerings go to the priest? “And the Lord spake unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.”

Aaron has no inheritance in the land; the Most High is his part and his inheritance. So the Lord’s heave offering of the spoil, given to Eleazar the priest, is the priesthood’s portion in place of land.

precepts.text: The children of Levi are given all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.
precepts.why:
“And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.”

Levi has no inheritance in the land either; the tenth in Israel is their inheritance, for the service of the tabernacle. The heave offering to Eleazar and the tenth to Levi are the same order: the Most High is their part, and the offerings of Israel sustain those who serve him.

precepts.text: These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass in the matter of Peor; that history stands behind this verse.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.
precepts.why:
“Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal–peor”. That recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite, and it was through his counsel that Israel fell: “Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.”

That history stands behind this verse. The plague is how “all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you.” But those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive: “ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day.”

The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25; go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.
A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow.
They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.
Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire.
They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.
Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive.

Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of Numbers 25.
Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to Numbers 5:2, putting the defiled outside the camp.
Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in Numbers 19.

Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites.
The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other.

A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.
